issues.description: The problem statement's UML for Stock shows take(String): int, but the template implementation declares Stock.take(String) returning boolean. The provided solution uses an int return value for take (returning -1 on failure) and SealSaloon logic (in the solution) expects an int result. This mismatch between the problem description, the template, and the solution will confuse students and prevent them from following the intended design and example solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and the solution by changing the signature of Stock.take(String) in the template to return int instead of boolean (e.g., return -1 when ingredient not found or insufficient quantity, otherwise return remaining quantity). Update any template comments or documentation to match this contract so students can implement SealSaloon logic consistent with the specification and solution.

issues.description: The Stock.take method's return type is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement UML specifies take(String): int, the solution's Stock.take returns an int (using -1 to indicate failure), but the template Stock.take is implemented as boolean take(String). This mismatch (same method name but different return type/semantics) creates a conceptual mapping problem for students following the UML and solution: they will expect an int result (and may write code that compares to -1) while the provided template method uses a boolean, causing confusion and compilation/behavior issues.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Stock.take signature with the UML and solution: change the template method to public int take(String ingredient) and implement the same integer return convention (e.g., return -1 on failure, otherwise return the remaining quantity). This ensures consistent semantics across problem statement, template, and solution.
